This is provenance description, and the same class has been graded SHOULD-FIX four times in this corpus as CLAUDE-PTLJ-V3-SF1, CLAUDE-DALJ-V7-SF1, CLAUDE-DALJ-V10-SF1 and CLAUDE-PLJ-V8-SF1. I am holding to that grading. What is new here is not severity but shape: this is the first instance where the defect accumulates across folds rather than recurring singly.

observationsNotFindings: The substantive re-pinning is done correctly and completely. Every governing value — top-level head, recordedInputs.HEAD, file08Pin.sha256 and file08Pin.head, and summary.requiredNowUnchanged — equals live, and the seven-obligation partition is byte-identical to frozen v5. This chain got right on its own the thing the exact-bytes chain needed a MUST-FIX to reach two subjects ago, and it disclosed the predecessor's historical standing without being asked.

The finding is worth stating as a shape rather than an instance. Four previous artifacts in this corpus carried one stale self-version sentence each; this one carries two, because the chain writes a fresh concrete claim at every fold and never revisits the older ones. That makes the count a function of fold depth. The doctor-actor and permission chains solved this by adopting a generic formulation, and every role using it has survived every fold — so the remedy is known and already in use elsewhere in the same corpus.

The five-entry liveGateOwners block is the widest I have checked and every entry matches its live cell. Owner blocks are where an invented value hid undetected for a full cycle earlier in this session, so a five-for-five result is worth recording rather than passing over.

decision.summaryForCoordinator: One SHOULD-FIX, no blockers. The re-pinning is done correctly and completely: top-level head, recordedInputs.HEAD, file08Pin.sha256 and file08Pin.head, and summary.requiredNowUnchanged all equal live by ==, no bare 26 or 27 appears anywhere, and the three surviving 5d5d778 references are each explicitly historical about frozen v5 and paired with the live value. The seven-obligation partition is byte-identical to v5 — same ids, same order, same flags, zero bodies changed — so the natural over-reach did not occur, and OBL-2, OD-101-1 and OD-101-2 all remain leftover-design. All 8 path-bearing pins and 17 recordedInputs recompute; all five liveGateOwners entries match their live cells, the widest owner block I have checked; no D-006 unit, MiB, 1048576 or 26214400 appears, and every Rust mention is a refusal. What lands is that predecessorJoin.v3.role still says 'This v4 does not reuse the v3 version number' and v4.role says 'This v5 …', both in a v6 artifact and both byte-identical to their frozen-v5 text. This is the fifth instance of this class in the corpus, but the first that accumulates: no role in this chain uses the immune generic form, so each fold writes a correct concrete claim for the newest predecessor and leaves the older ones stale — one at v5, two at v6, three at v7 unless the form changes. I graded SHOULD-FIX to match the four prior gradings, and the fix I recommend is the generic form rather than correcting to 'This v6', because the latter is right for one fold and leaves the accumulation in place. One note on method: my self-version scan produced a false positive on the previous subject, so I tightened it to discount version tokens qualified by another artifact's name before running it here; both hits survive that discount.
